name: axis-01-white-plate
version_tag: MECHANICAL CALENDAR AXIS — white plate: bolt + 2 nuts + washer, WHITE PLA BASIC (tray 0). Loaded as ONE object deliberately: PRINT_PLATE_white.stl is pre-arranged (bolt at 0,0; nuts at 34,-8 and 34,16; washer at 60,-8) and compose centres each object on its own bbox, so splitting it would destroy that layout. The brief asked for a split so support settings could be per-part — not possible here (this pipeline sets process options per PLATE, not per object) and not necessary: normal(auto) supports only generate material where an overhang actually demands it, so parts that need none get none. SUPPORTS ARE ON, and the measured overhangs justify it beyond the bolt: bolt 1925mm2, nuts 153mm2 EACH, washer 172mm2. The brief's claim that the nuts and washer are flat is wrong — they are chamfered. BRIM 8mm ADDED, NOT IN THE BRIEF, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. The bolt is 97mm tall on 380mm2 of contact, ratio 4 — worse than main-axis (5) and far worse than the month drum (79) which detached at layer 4 on cal-03 and was dragged into a spaghetti mess. The washer is worse still: chamfered both faces, so its true bed contact is 0.6mm2 (z=0) with the real 171.8mm2 face floating at z=0.59. Without a brim it does not stick, full stop. 4 walls and 35% infill per the brief (the calendar plates used 3 walls). Layer 0.20mm, stock 0.20mm Standard speeds — no quiet/fast preset.
